name: Friedrich Nietzsche
summary: Nietzsche attacked democracy, equality of rights, socialism, Christianity and the pity morality as signs of decline, and called for an aristocratic order of rank and new philosophers who would rear a higher type of man. He also scorned German nationalism, the Reich and anti-Semitism, wanted a united Europe of 'good Europeans', and treated war and struggle as sources of strength. His aphorisms are often ironic and ambiguous, so many policy questions have no stated answer.

unions-good.rationale: Listed the right of combination and voting among the mistakes that made the working man regard his condition as an injustice (Twilight, Skirmishes 40).

strong-leader.rationale: Called for a new ruling caste or commanders able to give Europe one will, ending petty-statism, and admired Caesar and Napoleon; but he also derided Prussian statism and national power-politics, so the fit with 'bypassing gridlock' is loose.

state-harmful.rationale: Zarathustra's 'New Idol' attacks the state as a lie and idol, yet Twilight (Skirmishes 39) laments the loss of authority and institutions and calls anarchists decadents, so he is not an anarchist; the evidence points both ways.

rehabilitation.rationale: Said we sin against criminals by treating them as rascals and that punishment should deter (Human, All Too Human 66, 105), yet also thought punishment tames and does not improve; mixed.

traditional-family.rationale: Defended marriage as an institution of lineage, heirs and solidarity over generations, and mourned its loss in modern society (Twilight, Skirmishes 39).

more-religion-public.rationale: Declared a 'war to the death' on the church and Christianity ('Christianity is the one great curse') and that democracy is 'Christian instinct' (Antichrist 62; Beyond Good and Evil 202).

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Valued tradition and institutions that last for centuries (Twilight, Skirmishes 39) but mocked national culture and the 'national' taste; mixed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Reported that Germans' instinct says 'Let no more Jews come in' and that 'one must act' on the instinct, while praising the Jews and urging expulsion of the anti-Semites in the same passage; irony makes this unclear.

nation-first.rationale: Rejected nationalism and race-hatred as 'blood-poisoning'; called himself a good European and attacked the 'névrose nationale' that divided Europe into petty states (Gay Science 377; Ecce Homo).

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred: treated revolution-ideologues and the anarchists as the herd's impatient wing and Christianity's 'dynamite'; did not discuss when revolution could be justified.

democracy-best.rationale: Called the democratic movement a degenerating form of political organisation and of man, and the democratising of Europe a breeding-ground for a type ready for slavery (Beyond Good and Evil 202-203, 242); also called democracy the decaying form of the state (Twilight, Skirmishes 39).

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: scorned the 'folly of the greatest number' and 'parliamentary imbecility' and held democracy to be decay, which excludes rule by popular vote on laws.

natural-rulers.rationale: Held that every elevation of the type man has come from an aristocratic society with a long scale of rank and differences of worth, and hoped for new philosophers and commanders to rule (Beyond Good and Evil 203, 257-258); praised the caste order as based on nature (Antichrist 57).

political-violence-never.rationale: Praised war and the warrior ('the good war halloweth every cause') and said freedom means readiness to sacrifice men, himself included.

war-builds-character.rationale: 'War trains men to be free'; 'the free man is a warrior'; 'war and courage have done more great things than charity' (Twilight, Skirmishes 38; Zarathustra, Of War and Warriors).

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Called the divine origin of law a 'holy lie' yet praised the Code of Manu as more intellectual and as ordering castes by nature (Antichrist 56-57); mixed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Described Europeans as mixing into a super-national type (Beyond Good and Evil 242), called nations res facta, not race, and urged advances to the Jews and absorption (Beyond Good and Evil 251); opposed race-hatred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Held equality to be bound up with a declining culture, and the 'pathos of distance' between classes necessary to elevation (Twilight, Skirmishes 37; Beyond Good and Evil 257).

self-interest-moral.rationale: Blessed 'wholesome, healthy selfishness that springeth from the powerful soul' as a virtue, and called selflessness a mark of decadence (Zarathustra, Of the Three Evil Things; Twilight).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Praised the will to tradition, authority and solidarity across centuries (Twilight, Skirmishes 39) but defended the free individual of the elite against the herd; mixed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Wrote that industrial civilisation 'in its present form is in general the meanest mode of existence that has ever been' (Gay Science 40).

conscription.rationale: In the Genealogy he calls universal military service an antidote to 'the effeminacy of democratic ideas', which is support for compulsory service.

positive-liberty.rationale: Defined freedom as the will to be responsible for oneself and to overcome resistance, and said liberal institutions undermine freedom (Twilight, Skirmishes 38); no mention of material means as a condition.

total-state.rationale: Zarathustra calls the state the coldest of all cold monsters, a lie whose creation is for the superfluous, and says the man who is not superfluous begins 'where the state ceases' (Of the New Idol).

territorial-expansion.rationale: Foresaw a 'struggle for the dominion of the world' and great politics, yet attacked the German Empire and nationalist state-building; no statement on a nation expanding its territory.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Developed a perspectival view that philosophers' truths serve their power and drives (Beyond Good and Evil preface, 6; Genealogy III), but his claim is not about the social power of a society; ambiguous.

universal-morality.rationale: Denied universal moral truths: master morality and slave morality, and 'every elevation of the type' depends on rank, not universal reason (Beyond Good and Evil 202, 260).

national-self-determination.rationale: Inferred: opposed nationalism, 'petty-statism' and the national state, and expected a supra-national European type (Beyond Good and Evil 242).

reason-over-faith.rationale: Attacked faith as an unwillingness to know, but also distrusted reason and pure objectivity and valued instinct (Beyond Good and Evil 208; Twilight); contested.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Held woman's 'first and last function' to be bearing robust children and that she should be preserved and protected, and that equal rights between the sexes do not exist (Beyond Good and Evil 239; Gay Science 363).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Inferred: welcomed the Jews' intermarriage with European nobility and urged making advances and absorption; segregation laws are not mentioned.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Wrote that society should ruthlessly suppress and eliminate 'degenerate life' in favour of 'the right of procreation' (Twilight, Skirmishes 36) and that 'the weak and ill-constituted shall perish' (Antichrist 2); this is aphoristic and does not specify state measures.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contested: Beyond Good and Evil ties depression to the crossing of too heterogeneous races, but he also said Jewish intermarriage with the noblest European blood would be beneficial. The remarks point both ways.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Called equal rights a decline, 'a pigmy with equal rights and claims'; denounced 'equality of souls before God' as Christian dynamite (Beyond Good and Evil 203, 257; Twilight, Skirmishes 37; Antichrist 62).

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred: held that every elevation of mankind came from an aristocratic order that rules and obeys, and that society exists as a scaffold for a select class, not to rest on consent; no direct discussion of legitimacy by consent.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rejected refraining from injury, violence and exploitation as a principle of society, calling it a denial of life, since life is essentially appropriation, injury and conquest (Beyond Good and Evil 259).

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Held that life is essentially appropriation and will to power and that elevation of the type comes from struggle and the pathos of distance between ranks; this is not a claim specifically about progress between peoples.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred: attacked pity and 'practical sympathy for the botched' as the harm greater than any vice (Antichrist 2, 7); no explicit statement on law priorities.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Lamented that nationalism had split Europe into petty states and asked who knows an aspiration great enough to bind its peoples together; wished for Europe to acquire one will (Ecce Homo; Beyond Good and Evil 208, 256). Neither mentions an institution like the EU.

clerical-rule.rationale: Said that 'hitherto the priest has ruled' and that the priest is a parasite on life who denies nature (Antichrist).

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ranked cultures and moralities: master versus slave morality, the Renaissance as the last great age, modern Europe a weak age; 'differences of worth between human beings' (Beyond Good and Evil 257, 260; Twilight, Skirmishes 37).

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Held that morality is obedience to custom and that 'the free man is immoral' because he depends on himself and not on tradition (Dawn 9); prized exceptions against the herd.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred: rejected the morality of pity and of mutual sympathy as decadence; no discussion of foreign aid.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred: said the Jews wish to be absorbed and settled in Europe and that Europe should make advances to them (Beyond Good and Evil 251); no statement on fighting for equal rights.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Inferred: opposed women entering politics and public affairs (Beyond Good and Evil 239).

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Defended a healthy aristocracy that keeps its privileges as the justification of the commonwealth and praised solidarity 'in long family lines'; opposed every 'special right' being levelled away.

patriotic-education.rationale: Treated patriotic national feeling as an 'atavistic' attack that leads to narrow tastes made 'national', and ridiculed the German Empire's 'Deutschland über alles' mentality (Beyond Good and Evil 241; Gay Science 377).

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Early work said animals are 'placed too far below the level of mankind' (Human, All Too Human), but later called compassion even for animals a feature of the democratic morality of sympathy (Beyond Good and Evil 202); contested.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Said the noble man helps the unfortunate 'not from pity' but from an impulse of abundant power, not out of duty (Beyond Good and Evil 260); contested.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Told his readers to withdraw from the state's idolatry and said 'the time for petty politics is past' (Zarathustra; Beyond Good and Evil 208); he also demanded 'great politics', so contested.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Said the rational basis of marriage lay in its absolute indissolubleness (Twilight, Skirmishes 39).

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Attacked the 'madness of nations' that wish above all to produce and be rich, and praised the freedom of the man who has few needs (Dawn 206).

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Said the Jews could have supremacy over Europe if they wished but 'that they are NOT working and planning for that end is equally certain', and that anti-Semitic bawlers should be banished (Beyond Good and Evil 251); an anti-Semite does not become respectable because he lies on principle (Antichrist 55).

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: lamented that modern marriage 'is being abolished' as it has lost its meaning.

religion-illusion.rationale: Regarded religion as a consoling fiction of the suffering, but traced its fall to loss of intellectual conscience, not to improved material conditions (Antichrist; Gay Science 125); contested.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: He argues that women's economic and legal independence as clerks, and the 'emancipation of woman', weakened women's most womanly instincts and were a symptom of decline.

assisted-dying.rationale: Wrote that 'in certain cases it is indecent to go on living', that death should be chosen freely at the right time, and that doctors are to help (Twilight, Skirmishes 36; Zarathustra, Of Voluntary Death).

alienated-labor.rationale: Said factory workers are used as 'the screws of a machine' and that higher wages would not remove their impersonal enslavement (Dawn 206).

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Held that authority arises from strength and from the order of rank and that law was given a divine origin as a priestly device (Antichrist 57); also said God is dead.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Told his 'brethren in war' to love 'peace as a means to new wars' and held that military civilisation stands above industrial civilisation (Zarathustra; Gay Science 40).

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: scorned the anti-Semitic movement ('folly'), broke with his publisher over anti-Semitism and suggested banishing the anti-Semites; boycotts are not mentioned.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Said the rational basis of marriage lay in the exclusive legal responsibility of the man (Twilight, Skirmishes 39).

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: celebrated war, the warrior and readiness to kill and to die, and opposed the morality of pity; did not speak of self-defence as such.

person-over-state.rationale: Contested: he said a healthy aristocracy must accept with a good conscience the sacrifice of a legion of individuals, but he also attacked the state as an idol and treated the individual's strength as the measure of value.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Wrote that it is 'the good war which halloweth every cause' and looked to a coming struggle for dominion of the world and 'great politics' (Zarathustra; Beyond Good and Evil 208).

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: preferred a Europe made threatening enough to acquire one will and valued danger as the nursery of strength (Beyond Good and Evil 208; Twilight, Skirmishes 38).

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: told his readers to love peace only as a means to new wars and to seek victory, so he would reject refusing to fight.

sacred-nation.rationale: Rejected national sentiment as a disease and 'national stupidities'; held that nationalism makes the German nation barren by making it vain (Gay Science 377; Ecce Homo).

shared-human-nature.rationale: Held that man is 'unexhausted' and a bridge to the Superman, to be reared by new philosophers and 'collective attempts in rearing' (Beyond Good and Evil 203; Zarathustra prologue).

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred: he contrasts religions by their values and sees Christianity as one decadent form among others rather than one shared truth.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Mocked women who aspire to 'the economic and legal independence of a clerk' as retrograde (Beyond Good and Evil 239); inheritance is not discussed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Denounced the 'emancipation of woman' as a symptom of decline and ridiculed advice to let women meddle with politics (Beyond Good and Evil 239). Voting is not named.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Treated the Bible and revelation as a 'holy lie' of the priests, and Christian faith as not wishing to know the truth (Antichrist, esp. 56-57).

simple-living.rationale: Praised 'a philosophy in rags' and the freedom of spirit of a man of few needs, and 'voluntary and idyllic poverty' for the intellectual (Dawn 206).

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred: held marriage should be indissoluble and responsibility the husband's alone (Twilight, Skirmishes 39).

notes:
Based on his published books only; his sister Elisabeth's Will to Power compilation and her nationalism are not used, and the notebook aphorisms appended to the Genealogy volume were set aside. Beyond Good and Evil 251 ('Let no more Jews come in') is ironic and surrounded by praise of the Jews and contempt for anti-Semites, so it is answered 0. Antichrist praise for the Code of Manu and Zarathustra's attack on the state pull in opposite directions for state and scripture statements (0). Applied-policy questions he never discussed are null.

Merged with an independent claude-haiku-5-5 audit: 3 answers taken from it, 24 agreed, 3 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-haiku-5-5 notes: Answers rest on his own published books, read as full text; aphorisms are ironic and sometimes voice opposing views, so ambiguous passages are low or 0. The Will to Power (edited by his sister) was not used. Many statements are null because his writings do not address them. Salience was not considered when answering.
